reviewer.origin: Agent tool, a fresh context with only this brief and its files, launched by the Inner Child lane session (https://claude.ai/code/session_01NbUfhcTaRT8sbjyYV1wEFq), turn 113, 2026-10-26

evidence: I judged "Which thoughts to talk to" over "I think a fear that keeps turning up to tell you something is worth talking to as a part of you..." and "I wouldn't spend long deciding what to call each part, though.": the first sentence answers the heading directly (a recurring fear yes; "a stray thought" and a worry that keeps asking to be reassured no, unless it's the little one), "thoughts" covers that fear, worry and stray thought, and it adds no claim. The second paragraph (naming, "it doesn't have to get any louder") is looser than the heading, but "though" ties it to the first, so one heading over both splits nothing, and the source's opening sentence "How you picture all that is up to you..." now closes the "If you do get an answer" paragraph, where "all that" has its antecedent. No linter findings and no writer-marked rows; T19, T24 and T26 are not happening (a reader's question answered flatly, "talk to" a plain shared verb), and the headings around it read as the exercise's real branches, not a tidy taxonomy.
